The [https://www.escoe.ac.uk/ Economic Statistics Centre of Excellence] (ESCoE) brings a research-led approach to measuring the economy. Established in 2017 with the support of the UK Office for National Statistics (ONS) and hosted at King’s Business School, ESCoE is a hub of expertise, supporting and delivering cultural change in the delivery of economic statistics.

The Centre brings together statistics producers, academics, policymakers and data users to analyse key economic issues and develop cross-functional solutions.

To do this, ESCoE has a network of Research Associates, PhD students and partner organisations who use advanced tools from economic theory, econometrics and data science, mathematics and statistics to advance economic measurement.<ref>{{cite web |date=September 11, 2025 |title=About ESCoE |url=https://www.escoe.ac.uk/about-escoe/ |publisher=ESCoE}}</ref>

== History ==
ESCoE was founded by a consortium of British university [[business school]]s, including [[Strathclyde Business School]], with the ONS in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.econ.cam.ac.uk/news/smith-ESCoE.html |title=Faculty of Economics - Economic Statistics Centre of Excellence - Richard Smith |publisher=University of Cambridge |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180822130132/http://www.econ.cam.ac.uk/news/smith-ESCoE.html
|archive-date=August 22, 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ons.gov.uk/aboutus/whatwedo/programmesandprojects/economicstatisticstransformation/economicstatisticscentreofexcellenceescoe |title=About Economic Statistics Centre of Excellence (ESCoE) |publisher=ONS }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.kcl.ac.uk/news/escoe-hosts-biennial-meeting-of-the-international-association-for-research-in-income-and-wealth |title=ESCoE hosts biennial meeting of the International Association for Research in Income and Wealth |date=October 9, 2025 |publisher=King's College London }}</ref>

It was originally housed at the [[National Institute of Economic and Social Research]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.niesr.ac.uk/escoe |title=ESCoE - Economic Statistics Centre of Excellence |publisher=NIESR |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202191924/https://www.niesr.ac.uk/escoe |archive-date=Feb 2, 2019 }}</ref> and is now based at King's Business School in central London.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About ESCoE |url=https://www.escoe.ac.uk/about-escoe/ |access-date=2025-09-11 |website=ESCoE |language=en-GB}}</ref>
== Research programme ==
ESCoE’s research areas include: labour markets and households; National Accounts; net zero, climate change and the environment; productivity, innovation and business dynamics; and Beyond GDP and inclusive wealth. The Centre also works on the measurement of time use, and a historical data repository and runs conferences, webinars, and workshops to inspire knowledge sharing and collaboration.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About ESCoE |url=https://www.escoe.ac.uk/about-escoe/ |access-date=2025-09-11 |website=ESCoE |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Leadership ==
ESCoE is led by Professor Rebecca Riley, and supported by Research and Enterprise Director Paul Schreyer, Operations Director Sarah Sheppard and Engagement Director Darren Morgan. ESCoE has a wider Leadership Executive representing key partner institutions and an Advisory Board drawn from government, the private sector, the media and international organisations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our people |url=https://www.escoe.ac.uk/people/ |access-date=11 September 2025 |publisher=ESCoE}}</ref>

== Partners ==
Partners include the ONS, King’s Business School, the Institute for Fiscal Studies, UNSW Sydney, and the universities of Cambridge and Strathclyde.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our partners |url=https://www.escoe.ac.uk/our-partners/ |access-date=2025-09-11 |website=ESCoE |language=en-GB}}</ref>
